# BAD-036 — Refactor every application code file over 1000 lines into smaller modules: Phase 1 extraction plans, Phase 2 implementation

## Brief
Eric's ask (2026-09-15): before any further feature work, refactor every application code file over 1000 lines into smaller modules, to make concurrent work and maintenance tractable. The size rule, clarified by Eric the same day: 250 lines is not a cap, it is the point at which a file gets looked at to see whether it is too large; a cohesive unit may be as large as it needs to be, and the larger it gets the harder that check is. Scope is application code only (Node, Deno, TypeScript, and any Python): stylesheets, HTML and test files are out. Two phases. Phase 1 is planning only: analyze each file's responsibilities (types, business logic and state, helper utilities, sub-components), propose a directory and file structure, list every planned new file and exactly what moves into it, and guarantee the original entry point keeps the exact same public surface so nothing that imports or script-loads it breaks. Eric approves the file layout before any code is written. Phase 2 is implementation, per file, in this order: shared types and pure utilities first, then state and services, then sub-components, then the entry file reduced to an orchestrator; verified with zero behaviour change.

Survey at the ticket's creation, tracked JS/TS files at or over 1000 lines, excluding node_modules, dist, vendored and fixture trees:

| File | Lines | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| renderer/app.js | 8991 | Electron renderer, plain script, no build step |
| main.js | 6724 | Electron main process |
| renderer/creator.js | 3044 | Electron renderer, plain script |
| web/app.js | 1909 | browser, plain script, copied into dist/web by build-web.js |
| admin/src/lib/accounts.ts | 1706 | Next.js admin dashboard, TypeScript |
| web/collabweb.js | 1580 | browser, plain script |
| scripts/build-release-notes-art.js | 1547 | Node script |
| web/booth.js | 1406 | browser, plain script |
| admin/src/lib/actions.ts | 1263 | Next.js admin, TypeScript |
| server/supabase/functions/collab/index.ts | 1230 | Deno Edge Function |
| admin/src/app/accounts/[email]/page.tsx | 1207 | Next.js admin, React page |
| scripts/web-api.js | 1005 | Node script |

Out of scope by Eric's call: the three stylesheets over 1000 lines (renderer/styles.css 3759, site/styles.css 2008, web/styles.css 1951), renderer/index.html (1057), the two server test files (test/server/functions.test.mjs 2416, test/server/schema.test.mjs 1221), and docs/superpowers/design/2026-09-03-mobile-handoff/support.js (a design artifact, not shipped code).

Constraints every plan must honour, from the repo's CLAUDE.md files:
- src/ stays plain Node with no Electron imports; main-process pieces cannot move there. The electron-builder files allowlist in package.json bundles only main.js, preload.js, src/**, renderer/**, brand assets and package.json, so any new directory the packaged app loads must be added to it or the release breaks.
- renderer/ has no build step: index.html loads plain classic scripts by tag, top-level bindings such as the `state` const and functions like selectPack are shared global scope, reached by later scripts, by the --smoke walkthrough in main.js, and over CDP. A split must keep them reachable under the same names and keep classic-script semantics (no ES modules) unless the plan proves otherwise. The renderer CSP is in force.
- web/ loads fourteen src/ modules by script tag, byte-identical, and scripts/build-web.js copies the tree and stamps URLs into dist/web; new files must be picked up by that build and by web/index.html.
- Shared rules (sceneBucket, isUnlimited and the rest) exist in pairs across src/, web/ and server/_shared; a refactor moves code, it never reimplements a shared rule.
- Verification is the implementing-changes skill's tier table: npm test for src/, a scoped npm run smoke for main.js and renderer/ (the creator over CDP), the server-changes skill for server/**, the admin's own lint and build for admin/.

Phase 1 plan: architect spudagents (fable) produce one spike per file at the Spud home under docs/spikes/bad-036/, each with the responsibility map, the proposed tree, the per-file move list, the entry-point compatibility argument, the verification recipe, and every proposed file over 250 lines with its honest size and the reason it stays whole, so Eric judges each one. Spud then creates one queued ticket per file with the spike as its brief. Eric approves the layouts; Phase 2 activates the tickets one worktree and PR each.

## Size, persona and model decision
Phase 1: architect spudagents on fable, up to three alive at once, one spike per file, scouts on haiku as children where a file is too big to hold; Phase 2: one engineer on opus per file ticket, a reviewer on fable for renderer/app.js and main.js.

## Outcome
Phase 1 complete on 2026-09-15: twelve extraction spikes in the Spud home under docs/spikes/bad-036/, one per application code file over 1000 lines, each with the ten sections (surface contract, responsibility map, proposed tree, entry point, files over 250, build touch points, verification, Phase 2 order, risks). Twelve queued P1 tickets carry them, BAD-041 to BAD-049 and the three admin tickets filed after them, each held for Eric's approval of its layout. None of the spikes has been reviewed by a second agent. Found on the way and queued as their own tickets: BAD-037, BAD-038, BAD-039, BAD-040 (P2, lands before the art split), and the two admin proposals. The Fable usage limit stopped the four Fable architects after they had written their spikes; web/collabweb.js was the one lost and was redone on opus. Nine tickets were first misfiled in the Spud project as SPD-067 to SPD-075 and declined with pointers to their badtakes copies.
